requirement:
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
rationale:
The two marked tests adequately cover `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.excerpts`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not read the implementation.

The requirement has three testable obligations.

**1. Excerpts, including matching and context text, are clipped to the identified item's span.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_excerpts_stop_at_byte_boundaries_including_attached_comments_and_attributes]` runs `ripgrep` with `context` 99 and `ast_grep` over a file with neighbouring items. These are `fn before`, `fn target`, `fn after` and `fn last`.
- It asserts that the output contains none of `unwanted_before`, `unwanted_after`, `unwanted_last` or `fn last`. With context 99, ripgrep would otherwise have pulled these in.
- It checks that the matches come back as exactly `fn[target]`, `fn[left]` and `fn[right]`.
- The same test also runs `ripgrep` with `context` 0 for `café` and for `inline`. It asserts one match, `fn[target]`, for `café`, and `fn[target]` and `fn[right]` for `inline`.
- The test redacts a token and checks it is absent. It also uses a multibyte character (`café`), which covers the byte-boundary aspect.
- `fn[exact_match_ranges_preserve_regex_anchors_and_skip_unmatched_or_binary_sources]` checks that the excerpt `lines` for `fn exact` are exactly the single matched line. It does this for several anchored and case-insensitive patterns with context 10. The context does not leak the following `fn last` or other files.

**2. The item's attached source (comments and attributes) is included, per `requirements.references.outline_comments`.**
- For `ripgrep` on `fn[target]`, the test asserts the excerpt contains `needle docs` (the doc comment), `#[inline]` (the attribute) and the body.
- The `needle docs` match belongs to `fn target` rather than a separate item.
- The `/* needle attached */` comment follows other source on its line. The test asserts it is attributed to `fn[left]`, which is included in left's lines, and is absent from right's lines.
- `#[inline] fn right` is asserted present in right's excerpt.

**3. Clipping applies within a line shared by different items.**
- The shared line holds `fn left`, the comment, `#[inline] fn right` and `fn last`.
- The test asserts that left's excerpt does not contain `fn right` and that right's excerpt does not contain `fn left` or `needle attached`.
- It also asserts that `fn last` appears nowhere. This is checked for both `ripgrep` and `ast_grep`.

I found no plausible violating behaviour that these assertions would accept. Both tools are exercised, and both the comment-match and code-match cases are covered. Context text, shared-line clipping and attached source each have an assertion. The remaining differences, such as other languages' attachment rules, belong to `requirements.references.outline_comments` and are not the subject here.

text: :::{req} search_accounting.excerpts
Every `ripgrep` or `ast_grep` excerpt, including matching and context text,
MUST be clipped to
the source span of the outline item identified by their `file` and `item`,
including that item's attached source under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Clipping MUST apply within a line shared by different items.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
